title: The Abstract painting
subtitle: 艺术殿堂 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）
meta: 主题语境：艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）　|　核心词汇：abstract　|　正文 329 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 abstract 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 the driver wrote of ① an abstract painting in the timetable, and everybody in the station said at once that it was ② more abstract than the one named there the year before. Three days on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the driver, who never explained anything, had done it in the rain and gone home; it was the abstract ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most abstract painting anybody in the station had ever seen, or so the timetable for February 1948 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too abstract to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the passenger who had come to help; the abstract ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the ticket at the far platform, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an abstract idea of duty, and said that no passenger in his right mind would call it ⑥ as abstract as the idea of duty they had once had in the old station. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was abstract or not, and he said so.

By 1961 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the timetable. What the line asked for was ⑦ something abstract, and nothing besides. The passenger from the next station called the whole plan ⑧ quite abstract; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the timetable kept the names of the abstract ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1964, without complaint, she wrote of another abstract painting in the same timetable, and the work, which took two days, seemed ⑨ more abstract than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most abstract idea of duty in the whole station, she said in 1966, was the one she could never quite name; the abstract ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 抽象（前置定语 an abstract painting：1954 年司机在时刻表里记下的那件抽象的油画）
B. adj. 抽象／深奥（比较级 more abstract than：文中两处，一处比油画，一处比预想）
C. adj. 抽象／深奥（最高级 the most abstract：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 抽象（表语 too abstract to do：母亲觉得它太抽象，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 深奥（前置定语 an abstract idea of duty：叔叔把整件事称作一桩深奥的概念）
F. adj. 深奥（同级比较 as abstract as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩责任的概念相比）
G. adj. 深奥（后置定语 something abstract：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 深奥（受程度副词修饰 quite abstract：那位乘客的评价）

items.q: The most abstract idea of duty in

answers.why: abstract 意为“抽象”，1954 年司机在时刻表里记下的是“一件抽象的油画”，此处作前置定语 an abstract painting。
abstract 意为“抽象”，此处用比较级 more abstract than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
abstract 意为“抽象”，时刻表上 二月 那行字说它是车站里最抽象的一件，故用最高级 the most abstract painting。
abstract 意为“抽象”，母亲认为这件东西“太抽象了，谁也用不上”，too abstract to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
abstract 意为“深奥”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩深奥的概念”，此处作前置定语 an abstract idea of duty。
abstract 意为“深奥”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩责任的概念一样深奥”，同级比较用 as abstract as。
abstract 意为“深奥”，时刻表上那半行字要的是“深奥的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something abstract。
abstract 意为“深奥”，邻车站来的那位乘客认为这套计划“相当深奥”，quite 修饰原级 abstract。
abstract 意为“深奥”，1964 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要深奥”，故用比较级 more abstract than。
abstract 意为“深奥”，母亲 1966 年说的是“整个车站里最深奥的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most abstract idea of duty。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1954 年，司机在时刻表里记下了一件抽象的油画。（an abstract painting）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更抽象。（more abstract than …）
母亲觉得它太抽象，谁也用不上。（too abstract to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩深奥的概念。（an abstract idea of duty）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩责任的概念一样深奥。（as abstract as …）
到了 1961 年，时刻表上只剩半行字：要的是一件深奥的东西。（something abstract）
answers: In 1954 the driver wrote of an abstract painting in the timetable.
Everybody said it was more abstract than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too abstract to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an abstract idea of duty.
He said nobody would call it as abstract as the idea of duty they had once had.
By 1961 the timetable asked for nothing but something abstract.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 abstract 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1954 the driver wrote of an abstract painting in the timetable, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most abstract painting in the station, or so the timetable says.
My mother thought it too abstract to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business an abstract idea of duty, and nobody argued with him.
The passenger from the next station called the plan quite abstract, and everybody laughed.
The abstract ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
